articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister reacts to ‘insensitivity’ from strangers after the ‘Jolene' singer passed away
articles.summary: Stella Parton expresses the family's grief over Dolly Parton's death, addressing insensitivity from strangers and calling for compassion and respect in her remembrance.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s sister, Stella Parton, opened up about how the family has been dealing with the singer’s demise. She also warned everyone against making inconsiderate comments. Sharing that she has faced a lot of “insensitivity from strangers” after her sister left for her heavenly abode, Stella detailed how the Parton family is taking on all of the challenges altogether.Stella Parton opens up about how she has been dealing with things after Dolly Parton’s demiseThe 77-year-old singer-songwriter recently shared an Instagram post detailing how many people posted insensitive comments after her sister, Dolly Parton's, passed away. She expressed her gratitude for the people who have been wishing well for the family and actually showed up.She wrote, “First let me say, thank you to the ones of you who have shown ‘genuine’ support and love during this time of our family bereavement. We will be okay in time, but each of us will grieve in our own personal way. Every human being experiences pain and loss in life, and my family is no different.”She further added, “Sadly, because of the way our lives have been lived in front of the public, we have no choice but to be subjected to incredible pressure and insensitivity from strangers.”Stella Parton asks people to make a change in their lives and get inspired by Dolly PartonFurther down the post, she finally shared that people need to learn some compassion in their everyday life. She wrote. “Finally, I ask that you show more compassion and wisdom as we move forward in life. Use my sister’s life as an example for tolerance and respect toward others. It’s not about the most clever comments, fake AI garbage, or snarky tweets.”She concluded her post by adding, “That being said, I’ve always embraced my own personality and will continue to be myself and express my opinions as I deem appropriate regardless of what anyone thinks of me. It’s my right as a human being! Have a happy and safe weekend.”Dolly Parton passed away on August 25 after battling cancer. The singer had not revealed her health issues until after her passing. A statement from her representatives shared with PEOPLE revealed that the iconic star had left for her heavenly abode while she was admitted to a cancer facility, surrounded by family and loved ones. Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, was one of the first ones to inform everyone about Parton’s demise, sharing a video on all of her accounts.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Taapsee Pannu CALLS OUT Bollywood's obsession with 'same actors': 'All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same'
articles.summary: Taapsee Pannu has never shied away from calling out patterns she sees in the film industry. In her latest chat, she took aim at something many viewers.
articles.body: Taapsee Pannu has never shied away from calling out patterns she sees in the film industry. In her latest chat, she took aim at something many viewers have quietly noticed too: Bollywood films starting to feel repetitive because the same faces keep showing up in the same kind of stories. The actor, known for choosing offbeat and gritty roles, spoke candidly about how typecasting isn't just an actor's problem but a casting problem that filmmakers need to fix.Same actors, same genres, says Taapsee PannuSpeaking to Hindustan Times, Taapsee Pannu pointed out that Bollywood keeps recycling a small pool of actors for particular genres, which she believes is the real reason so many films end up looking alike. According to her, when studios rely on the same handful of stars for romance or glamour and another fixed set for thrillers, originality naturally takes a hit.She explained, "All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same because there are only those four or five actors, actresses who are doing that. All our thrillers look and feel the same because there are only those four or five actors who are doing that."She added that true novelty on screen requires filmmakers to be bolder with their choices. She said, "If you really want your film to look different, something new, something different, then you need to cast people who can bring that difference on screen."Costume changes don't erase the old image, says Taapsee PannuTaapsee Pannu also touched on how simply changing an actor's look or outfit doesn't automatically make a role feel fresh, since audiences already carry a fixed impression of that performer. She said, "If I've seen someone in a glamorous role, now you make that person wear a sari or a bikini or whatever, I have seen the glamour of that actor. It's only different, right?” she said, adding, “So that's not the fault of that poor actor, also."Taapsee Pannu on being typecast herselfTurning to her own journey, Taapsee Pannu acknowledged that she too has become synonymous with intense, hard-hitting characters, largely because those are the scripts she keeps receiving. She reasoned that picking the strongest script from a limited set only reinforces the label further. She said, "If you only offer me 10 intense films, I will choose the best out of them and present that, but it will still be a strong woman, intense film because that's the only genre that people have started imagining me."More about Taapsee Pannu's upcoming film 'Gandhari'Taapsee's remarks come alongside the release of her latest film, 'Gandhari', directed by Devashish Makhija and written and produced by Kanika Dhillon. She plays Bani, a mother whose life turns upside down after her daughter is kidnapped, pushing her into the eerie town of Joypurra and its unsettling Behrupiya lore. Ishwak Singh, Jatin Sarna, Swastika Mukherjee, Mita Vashisht, and Chhaya Kadam also star. The film began streaming on Netflix on September 3.Give your child the gift of confidence!
